seasonMovement: Impossible arrival -> settlement -> navigation -> participation -> belonging -> usefulness -> chosen household -> self-defined belonging under judgment.
seasonDramaticShift: Issues 1–5 are driven largely by collision with 2026 and the work of building an ordinary life. From Issue 6 forward, modern systems remain real pressure but stop being the default dramatic protagonist. The later season is driven by what these particular people want from work, one another, New York, autonomy, responsibility, and belonging.

kinContinuity.composition: Two men and Astrid, the only woman.
kinContinuity.issues1To3: The three Kin are seen primarily together in or immediately around the Bushwick placement; they are not yet followed independently around the city.
kinContinuity.middleSeason: Their independent errands, relationships, routines and interests begin to appear individually.
kinContinuity.issues6To7: Astrid is deliberately largely absent from foreground action while the two male Kin remain visible. Her absence is ordinary, not mysterious.
kinContinuity.issue8: The hearing reveals that Astrid has quietly built a robust independent ordinary life outside the parts of New York Carrie and Bjorn were tracking.
kinContinuity.maleNames: Personal names remain unresolved and intentionally unlettered through Issues 7–8. Current production identities are First Male Kin / @vik.KinMan1 and Second Male Kin / @vik.KinMan2; this does not block production.

issues.title: Trial of Toil
issues.function: Bjorn's crisis over usefulness becomes a character story about respect, consent, responsibility and meaningful contribution. The support group changes his behavior, but the revised middle tests that change through distinct situations—emergency action, shared household obligation, ordinary belonging, difficult advice, emotional witnessing and trust—rather than repeated requested-help exercises.
issues.status: structural tightening complete; active 24-page RexPrompt payload updated; dialogue line-polish pending

issues.title: War Council
issues.function: A Status Reconciliation Review forces the household to confront different wants without reducing them to one household doctrine. The city excursions make those wants concrete; the final council prepares five people to answer for themselves while leaving permanence, kinship, integration and Astrid's practical competence for the hearing to discover.
issues.status: Issue 8 discovery-preservation pass complete; active 24-page RexPrompt payload updated; dialogue line-polish pending

issues.title: Permanent Residency / Trial by Combat
issues.function: The Status Reconciliation Review exposes a genuine defect in the emergency intake record: Bjorn is still listed as the household responsible adult and the other four adults are carried derivatively, which cannot simply become five individual permanent statuses. The applicants must establish separate adult lives in the room; Carrie must correct her old casework assumption; Bjorn must surrender the last formal residue of authority before the Hearing Officer can grant five individual permanent temporal-resident statuses. Astrid's independence proof is deliberately compressed to three pages.

finaleState.ordeal: Issue 8 residency hearing functions as Bjorn's trial by combat through a genuine record defect: the emergency file still encodes him as the responsible adult for four other adults, and permanent status cannot issue individually until that hierarchy is tested and corrected.
finaleState.hearingPurpose: The institution must decide whether the emergency household classification still describes reality. The hearing can grant five individual permanent statuses only if the applicants establish separate adult agency and the old Bjorn-centered record is lawfully corrected.
finaleState.bjorn: Bjorn arrives in armor without weapons. His decisive act is not a speech: when the Hearing Officer explains that correcting the record removes his formal authority to answer for the others, he says, 'Then correct it.'
finaleState.carrie: Carrie admits she selected Bjorn as responsible adult during emergency intake because the system required one and he could answer enough questions. She earns the result by acknowledging that the designation became inaccurate and supporting five separate permanent findings.
finaleState.astrid: Astrid's independence is proven compactly in three pages through self-advocacy, navigation, errands, neighborhood relationships, and the distinction between mutual reliance and legal dependency. The hearing does not rank her or spend seven pages proving the point.
